facts.claim: Immigration and Civil Status Seychelles, FAQ 'Marriage Registrar': the marriage certificate issued by the Civil Status office of Seychelles is a legal document and is valid worldwide; before leaving the country, couples should ensure the certificate is apostilled by the Seychelles Supreme Court and issued with a letter of authentication by the Seychelles Ministry of Foreign Affairs. (Read live by the orchestrator, 17 November 2026.)

Immigration and Civil Status Seychelles, FAQ 'Marriage Registrar': all documents issued overseas must be translated into English or French and be apostilled. (Read live by the orchestrator, 17 November 2026.)

Immigration and Civil Status Seychelles, FAQ 'Marriage Registrar': documents for a wedding between foreigners: birth certificates of both parties; death certificate of a previous spouse if widowed; divorce certificates if applicable; clear passport copies of both parties; a duly filled marriage application form. (Read live by the orchestrator, 17 November 2026.)

Immigration and Civil Status Seychelles, FAQ 'Marriage Registrar': wedding registration is made in the office and both parties should be present; the age to marry is 18 and over. (Read live by the orchestrator, 17 November 2026.)

Immigration and Civil Status Seychelles, FAQ 'Marriage Registrar': the banns are published for 11 days before the date of marriage; this period may be exempted by applying for a special marriage licence, normally issued within two days of the application, and a fee applies. (Read live by the orchestrator, 17 November 2026.)

Immigration and Civil Status Seychelles, FAQ 'Marriage Registrar': foreigners may contact the Civil Status office at Independence House (Victoria, Mahé) or by email, or make arrangements through a local wedding agent or their hotel or place of accommodation, to register their wedding eleven days in advance. (Read live by the orchestrator, 17 November 2026.)

Immigration and Civil Status Seychelles, FAQ 'Marriage Registrar': a fee applies when both parties are foreigners, on Mahé, Praslin and La Digue and at a higher rate on other islands; on other islands the couple also bears the Civil Status Officer's transport, accommodation and meals. (Read live by the orchestrator, 17 November 2026.)
